spec.concept: Gravity causes all falling objects near the Earth to accelerate at a constant rate regardless of their mass, neglecting air resistance.
spec.definition: Falling objects are objects that move downward under the sole influence of gravity, accelerating as they fall.

prediction.prompt: You drop a rock off a tall cliff (ignore air). How many meters has it fallen after 4 seconds?

extremes.watch: On the Moon, gravity is much weaker, so the fall distance in 4 seconds is far smaller.
With extreme gravity, the distance grows rapidly because distance depends on the square of time.

misconceptions.label: Speed and distance mixed up
misconceptions.why_tempting: Gravity adds about 9.8 m/s each second, so 4 x 9.8 = 39 feels right.
misconceptions.refutation: 39 m/s is its speed at 4 s; distance is 1/2 g t squared = 78 m.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: Final speed times time
misconceptions.why_tempting: Multiplying speed by time is how distance usually works.
misconceptions.refutation: It started at rest, so its average speed is half the final speed: 19.6 m/s x 4 s = 78 m.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
